September 2, 2026

US launches new wave of strikes on Iran as Tehran hits bases across the region

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy, @aaronparnas

U.S. Central Command said it completed a wave of strikes on September 1 against Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets including air defence sites, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites. Trump said the strikes near the Strait of Hormuz were retaliation for an Iranian attempt to lay sea mines in the strait and for eight missiles fired at a U.S. base in Jordan, and warned of a larger attack still to come. Iran struck back at American bases across the Middle East in the largest exchange since July. Trump separately said he was not seeking to force Iran to the negotiating table, citing near-total control of the Hormuz Strait and a collapsing Iranian economy, and asked when the Iranian people would rise up and fight.

Iranian officials say US strike hit a wedding, killing at least five

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Iranian officials accused the United States of striking a wedding in an Iranian province, saying at least five people were killed and dozens injured, with several children among the casualties. Tehran characterised the strike as a war crime. The claim came as the two countries traded their heaviest strikes in weeks.

Russia said to be helping Iran build supersonic missiles able to target US warships

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

According to the Financial Times, Russia is providing Iran with advanced intelligence and technical support to develop supersonic cruise missiles capable of striking American warships in the Middle East. The transfer is described as one of the most significant movements of military technology from Moscow to Tehran known so far. The reporting cuts against Trump's public characterisation of his relationship with Vladimir Putin.

Hegseth faces impeachment calls as Army readiness reportedly suffers

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Multiple members of Congress, including Sarah McBride and Robert Garcia, said over the past 24 hours that they would support impeaching and removing the Secretary of Defense. CNN reporting cited internally is said to show that his focus on culture-war priorities is impeding Army progress, and he has pushed out generals who disagreed with him. Army officials have been resigning amid the turmoil.

Republicans move to send Congress home ahead of Epstein files vote

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A second discharge petition has been filed for the Epstein Files Transparency Act 2.0, legislation that would criminalise certain conduct by Department of Justice personnel and allow survivors to sue the department over failures including improper redaction. The petition has 37 signatures of the 218 needed. Thomas Massie, who read the names of 14 alleged Epstein co-conspirators on the House floor, said there are rumours Speaker Mike Johnson wants members out of Washington quickly, potentially until after the midterm elections, to avoid the vote.

Election administration concerns mount 62 days before midterms

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

A USPS official has blown the whistle on the Trump administration, accusing it of violating a court order and rapidly building a system that could produce catastrophic results in the midterm elections. Tarrant County, Texas voted to cut 92 polling sites for the midterms, and voter rolls are being purged in Texas. Concerns were also raised about certification of results and seating of winners, citing the delayed swearing-in of Representative Adelita Grijalva of Arizona in October 2025. Ed Markey won his Senate primary in Massachusetts.

ICE launches AI social media scanning program with contractor ZeroFox

tags: surveillance, immigration, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

An internal agency-wide memo describes a new ICE 'Doxing Mitigation Initiative' using the AI cybersecurity firm ZeroFox to scan social media and the dark web for information that could identify ICE agents and officers. ICE entered a roughly $14.6 million contract with ZeroFox last month, funded through ICE Intelligence, for a platform combining threat intelligence, brand and domain protection, and attack surface intelligence. Insiders and outside experts said the technology could also be used to identify whistleblowers and non-loyalists inside the agency. ZeroFox previously drew criticism over its use during the 2015 Baltimore protests and after the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

Cubans in Florida deported to African countries under third-country policy

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

According to the Tampa Bay Times, the Trump administration is deporting Cubans living in Florida to countries in Africa under its third-country removal policy rather than returning them to Cuba. The practice extends to undocumented immigrants nationwide, who are being sent to countries where they have no ties. Miami's Cuban community, which voted heavily for Trump, is now seeing its members removed under the policy.

Oil jumps more than $4 a barrel on renewed US-Iran fighting

tags: markets, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Oil prices surged more than $4 a barrel as renewed fighting between the United States and Iran raised fears of further supply disruptions. The move followed strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for global crude.

Patagonia and tribal groups sue Trump over Bears Ears reduction

tags: climate, legal, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Patagonia joined A'Nuche, a nonprofit led by members of the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe, and the Conservation Lands Foundation in a federal lawsuit in Washington challenging the shrinking of Bears Ears National Monument. Trump signed a proclamation in July cutting 91 percent of Bears Ears, more than 1.2 million acres, and reduced Grand Staircase-Escalante by nearly 1.7 million acres, or 90 percent. The suit argues the Antiquities Act allows a president to create monuments but not to shrink them. Companies have already staked at least nine mining claims in areas removed from the two monuments, and the changes opened the land to oil drilling and uranium mining.

Forest Service moves to repeal Roadless Rule covering 44 million acres

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The federal government is moving to repeal the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule, which bars most new road construction, road reconstruction and timber harvesting across roughly 44 million acres of national forest. Repeal would not automatically open the land to logging but would remove a national safeguard and shift decisions to individual forest plans. Roadless forests supply drinking water, wildlife habitat and stored carbon, and roads fragment habitat and open areas to further industrial activity. The proposal is in a public comment period during which the Forest Service must respond to comments on the record.

Nepal flood recovery funding arrives largely as debt

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A glacier collapse in the Himalaya on August 26 sent water, ice and rock down river valleys, killing nearly 1,000 people and leaving about 4,200 missing, with roads, bridges and whole villages destroyed. The United States first announced $500,000 in emergency assistance and the State Department later said $3.6 million in humanitarian aid had been activated, including food support for up to 10,000 households. The World Bank has indicated it could mobilise up to about $164 million, but as loans that would add to Nepal's debt. Advocates are calling for grants, debt relief and loss-and-damage finance instead, noting Nepal's economy is roughly $49 billion and average income about $1,660 a year, while ICE and Border Patrol hold $183 billion and the war in Iran has cost $37.5 billion by the Pentagon's count.

Super El Nino drives three Pacific storms and shifts US weather risks

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas

A super El Nino has intensified hurricane season in the Pacific Ocean, with three storms currently churning and all expected to reach hurricane strength. The BBC reports the pattern could bring greater storm surge and intense flooding to areas of California, while the Pacific Northwest and Canada face higher drought risk from reduced snowfall, raising wildfire danger and temperatures. The event is expected to produce more Pacific hurricanes, fewer Atlantic hurricanes, and significant harm to Pacific marine life.

Supreme Court to decide whether Second Amendment protects AR-15 ownership

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Supreme Court will hear a case on whether the Second Amendment protects ownership of AR-15 rifles. Gun owners brought the challenge seeking constitutional protection for the weapons.

Trump renames Lake Ontario and floats Strait of Trump

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Apple Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America for U.S. users following Google Maps, after Trump personally called Apple; MapQuest has not made the change and is currently the top app in the U.S. App Store. Trump posted about the renaming overnight, drawing complaints from his own supporters asking instead for lower healthcare and prescription costs. He has since suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz the Strait of Trump and floated renaming the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, following earlier changes to the Gulf of Mexico and the Department of Defense. No order has been signed for the latest proposals.

Vance draws criticism over end times remarks and loyalty pledge

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Vice President J.D. Vance said on a podcast that he would not be shocked if the country is living in the end times, and that he is focused on doing as much of God's work as possible even if that leads to the end times. The remarks drew confusion and debate from commentators on both the right and left. Vance made the comments during a tour for his new book, Communion. Separately, leaked audio circulated of Vance telling a group that the administration from the top down would always be on their team.

Republican Jewish Coalition says it led effort to defeat Thomas Massie

tags: politics, media
sources: @ericmoutsos

Norm Coleman, a former U.S. senator, said the Republican Jewish Coalition played the lead role in defeating Congressman Thomas Massie in his primary, stating that a Republican who votes against Israel does not get a pass, and that the group has publicly taken on Tucker Carlson by name. Coleman also said a majority of Gen Z holds an unfavourable view of Israel, attributing it to losing the digital information war, and named several technology executives while describing them as the people who set the terms of that battle. The remarks were circulated as confirmation of longstanding claims about coordinated pressure against figures who raised the Epstein case.

Brian Mast under consideration for Secretary of the Army

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual, @ericmoutsos

Defense officials say Congressman Brian Mast, an IDF veteran who wore an IDF uniform in the halls of Congress, is being considered to replace Dan Driscoll as Secretary of the Army. Sean Parnell and Derrick Anderson are also under consideration. Mast has publicly said that supporters of terrorists should be killed and has disputed the existence of innocent Palestinian civilians.

Trump nominates Hung Cao as Secretary of the Navy

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump announced he is nominating Hung Cao to serve as the next Secretary of the Navy, praising his work over the past four months and urging the Senate to confirm him quickly. Cao would lead the Navy and Marine Corps.

USS Abraham Lincoln arrives in Thailand showing heavy wear after nine months at sea

tags: defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The USS Abraham Lincoln pulled into Thailand after nine months at sea with visible rust and hull deterioration from prolonged saltwater exposure. Sailors aboard faced food rationing during the extended deployment, and some service members sought to leave the ship to avoid it. The crew has a five-day rest period before returning to the United States. Pattaya authorities have placed Soi 6, Soi 6/1 and Soi 7 off-limits to U.S. Navy personnel during the Chon Buri port visit from September 2 to 6, with more than 5,000 sailors expected in the area.

82nd Airborne deployments extended to a full year in the Middle East

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Some 82nd Airborne troops could spend up to a full year deployed in the Middle East under extended deployment orders. The extension comes amid escalating operations against Iran.

Putin envoy warns Russian war economy risks overheating

tags: markets, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

An envoy for Vladimir Putin warned that Russia's economy risks going into what he described as berserk mode if too much of it is devoted to the war effort. The comments point to strain from sustained military spending.

CDC removes two measles deaths from national database

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The CDC has scrubbed two measles deaths from its national database. The removal comes amid broader scrutiny of federal public health data reporting.

First responders diverted from national parks days before deadly Grand Canyon floods

tags: politics, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration diverted 300 specialized emergency first responders from national parks to work on a project in Washington, D.C. Days later, flash floods in the Grand Canyon killed at least two people.

Judge rules Tyler Robinson will stand trial in killing of Charlie Kirk

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A judge ruled that Tyler Robinson can proceed to trial in the killing of Charlie Kirk. Robinson faces the death penalty if convicted.

Lindsay Clancy jury deadlocked after 27 hours of deliberation

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The jury in the Lindsay Clancy trial reported for a second time that it cannot reach a unanimous verdict after 27 hours of deliberation, and the judge delivered a Tuey-Rodriguez charge, the Massachusetts version of an Allen charge, instructing them to continue. Court TV reported that jurors appeared frustrated when receiving the additional instruction. If the jury reports it is hopelessly deadlocked again, a mistrial would be declared and prosecutors would decide whether to retry the case and on what charges. The nature of the deadlock, including whether it concerns guilt or the degree of the offence, is not known.

Fox News segment blames falling fertility rate on teenagers not having children

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A Fox News segment argued that the decline in births among 15 to 19 year olds is a problem for the national fertility rate, noting the rate for that age group is down 7 percent recently and 70 percent over the last two decades. The commentary framed messaging encouraging young people to wait for financial stability before having children as a cause. The segment drew criticism for treating teen pregnancy rates as a policy shortfall.
